$comment: NEW-1 (plan 3.7): the EXACT issue lifecycle a session drives, ONE rule ×4 (TS reference packages/domain-contract/src/issue-lifecycle.ts; the server applies it in lib/sessions/issue-lifecycle.ts; the natives move no status and only mirror the table when they render it, NEW-7). issueLifecycleTarget(event, state) = the ANCHOR status the issue moves to, or null = nothing moves. Events: `taken` = a WORKER session takes the issue: a session_issues row lands on a session that has a repository (`worker`: its branch comes at claim) through a link, issueIds on a start, a forward, a continuation, or a PERSON's message into such a session that holds it (bus rows never count); `pr_opened` = a PR links it; `pr_merged` = that PR landed in the default branch (#FEED-207: a PR merged into its stack parent's branch AFTER that parent landed never reached it: nothing moves); `unlinked` = a worker dropped it; `filed` = a session CREATED the issue (EXP-1377: only when the create names it, sessionId or link: true = the caller's own; a create without either files an UNLINKED issue, never the caller's session by default): the row lands on the filer so the PR's share and the chat strip carry it, but filing is not working on it: nothing moves, in every state (the N-10 rule: an issue goes to In progress only when a session really takes it up). A later start, forward, link or a person's message into the filer takes it like any other row. State: `status` = the issue's anchor status (contract issueStatus), `openPr` = a live (open or draft) PR links it, `workers` = how many live sessions with a repository still hold it AFTER the event. Nothing else moves status: no settle-back when work stops, no move for a row on a session without a repository, no move on a message from a session. done, cancelled and duplicate never move here (people own them; a merge is the only automation into done). The team's PR automation (prOpened/prMerged targets, 'do nothing') maps the pr_* targets onto its rows as before; taken/unlinked always target the builtins. #EXP-1707 (merge-train.json LANDING): the merge train fast-forwards the base to the tested train commit and closes each landed PR on GitHub (it shows Closed there): that landing IS `pr_merged` for every PR of the landed unit (the worker applies it itself, merged_at = the fast-forward), and the `closed` webhook of a PR the train landed never counts as a close. conflict, failing and held move nothing: the PR stays live, its issues stay in_review.

reconcile.$comment: EXP-1706: a lost `closed`/`reopened` delivery must never strand an issue. Every watchdog tick (cloud AND self-hosted, beside the GITHUB_POLLING poller) re-reads the STATE (merged, closed, reopened, base; then unsettled checks) of live PRs whose row has not changed for `staleMinutes`, each at most once per `staleMinutes`, oldest first, at most `batch` reads per tick, skipped while the repository's installation budget is low (like the checks sweep). A merge it sees is applied like the webhook's (pr_merged moves the closing links). Provider-neutral: the forge read is one call per PR.

links.$comment: EXP-1706: the issues a PR LINKS (pull_request_issues; they take pr_opened/pr_merged above). prLinks(input) = `issueIds` (the opener's explicit ids, as identifiers) ∪ the head branch's trailing ident (`exp/EXP-12`, `feature/MET-3`) ∪ EVERY ident in the title prefix (`EDE-13, EDE-14: …`, `EXP-1662: EXP-1662: …` once; idents are an UPPERCASE prefix, a dash, digits; separators `,` `&` `+` `/` `and`; a leading `#` is allowed) ∪ the idents of every body line that starts with a closing keyword (`Fixes`, `Closes`, `Resolves` and their -ed/-es forms, any case, an optional list bullet: `Closes #EXP-12, #EXP-13`) ∪ the session's share. The share (pr-issues `prDefaultIssueIds`) joins ONLY when `issueIds` is omitted (explicit ids override it) and is NEVER the whole chat: a child's = its subtree's rows plus the idents its brief names (#EXP-1402); the root's = the rows it holds that no other session of the chat holds. Any other ident (the body's prose, a commit message body) is only a reference: it never links. Order = that union's order, each ident once, uppercase. `close` = `link` minus `parents` (issues with sub-issues): a parent is linked, but its own PR never moves it; it ROLLS UP (EXP-1334) once every one of its sub-issues reached the event's stage (opened: in review or beyond; merged: done, cancelled or duplicate), carried by a PR that links it as closing whose event (opened: the link; merged: the landing) is NEWER than the last status a PERSON set on it (#FEED-236: a person's move outranks an older PR: an issue a merged PR already closed, reopened by a person and then given sub-issues, never closes again on a sub-issue's merge; only a PR linking it after the reopen carries it). `pr unlink` never deletes a link: the row stays as a REFERENCE (server-only `closes = false`, hidden from clients) that no event moves; it answers `unlinked: true` (`already: true` when the row was a reference before), re-renders the PR body, and ERRORS when the PR never linked the issue; naming the issue in a later `issueIds` closes it again (a share re-link does not). Provider-neutral: no forge-specific syntax beyond the keywords.

trash.$comment: #EXP-1797: an issue's DELETE is a soft delete into the team's issue trash, on every surface (tRPC issues.delete + bulkDelete, MCP issues_write {op: delete}, an app's exponential.issues.delete: they all reach the same writer). Delete stamps `issues.deleted_at` + `deleted_by` (the member) + `deleted_by_agent_id` (the acting agent, null for a person) and NOTHING cascades: comments, files, labels, relations, subscribers, activity, session and PR links stay attached. A trashed issue is hidden from every read: the issues shape (static predicate `deleted_at IS NULL`), every child shape (the child rows' `board_deleted_at` trash mirror now means 'its container is in the trash': the board's OR the issue's own deleted_at; an issue relation is hidden while EITHER side is trashed), search, boards, inbox, chats' issue strips and MCP reads (an identifier or id of a trashed issue answers Issue not found), except the explicit trash reads: tRPC issues.listDeleted, MCP issues {op: trash}. `retentionDays` after deleted_at the watchdog's trash sweep (every tick, beside the app-records purge) PURGES it: the hard delete that cascades like the old delete and reclaims its files. RESTORE (members, `access.restore`; tRPC issues.restore, MCP issues_write {op: restore}) clears the three columns: the issue comes back with its identifier (numbers are never reused), comments, relations and links intact. DELETE FOREVER (`access.purge` = owners only; tRPC issues.purge, from the trash only) purges it now, after the `purge-issue` prompt (prompts.json). A trashed board's issues are not listed (the board's own trash restores them). EVENTS on the team stream (contract events.builtinNames), payload = `eventPayload`: `issue.deleted` and `issue.restored` (emittedBy the session when an MCP call speaks for one, else the person; viaMcp = the call came over MCP; actorAgentId = the acting agent), `issue.purged` (emittedBy the person for Delete forever, the server for the sweep, actor fields null then). THE TRASH VIEW ×4 = the team settings Boards page (where the board trash already lives, settings-boards): a `copy.band` band under the board bands, drawn only while non-empty, for EVERY member (the board bands stay owner-only), the same put-away row as a trashed board: the issue's board glyph, `copy.row` (flex, truncates), the caption `trashCaption(purgeAt, now)` (re-rendered every minute), then the `copy.restore` pill and, for owners only (`trashActions(role)`), the `copy.purge` pill. Rows newest deleted first. Loaded when the page opens and after every Restore / Delete forever; a failed load is quiet (the band keeps its rows), a failed Restore / Delete forever = the platform's toast, and the list reloads either way. Issue delete confirms = prompts.json delete-issue / delete-issues (Move to trash), Delete forever = purge-issue.
